columns.rationale: Order identifier with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 4000 over 5000 rows, samples such as 'ORD-100001' and 'ORD-100010' show a stable ORD-prefixed code; renamed from 'Order ID' to snake_case.
Landed INTEGER with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_values 1 through 7 (min 1, max 7), consistent with a line position within an order; renamed from CamelCase 'LineNo'.
null_rate 0.0 with distinct_count 320; samples mix numeric-looking codes ('10002', '85123A') with non-numeric entries ('BANK CHARGES', 'DOT'), so the column stays text.

Samples disagree on form: '-3', '12', '2.0' and the word 'three' appear among 41 distinct values, so no numeric cast is supported and the landed text is retained; null_count 10 (null_rate 0.002) is kept as null.
Landed DECIMAL(38,9) with null_rate 0.0, min -5.0 and max 1250.0; every sample value ('-5.0', '0.42', '2.55', '7.5') carries at most two decimal places, so DECIMAL(10,2) holds the range without loss.
null_rate 0.0 with distinct_count 1880; all ten samples are ISO-shaped ('2024-01-05 09:15:00' through '2024-01-09 12:12:00'), so the VARCHAR is cast to TIMESTAMP.

Across 44 distinct values the samples use incompatible formats ('01/07/2024', '07.01.2024', '2024-01-07', '2024-1-9', 'Jan 9 2024') plus the sentinels '' and 'TBD', so no date cast is defensible; renamed with a _raw suffix and null_count 1320 (null_rate 0.264) retained.

Sparsely populated: null_count 4850 of 5000 rows (null_rate 0.97) with only 140 distinct values such as 'a.customer@example.com'; the column is retained as nullable text rather than imputed or dropped.

Free-text operator notes, null_count 3050 (null_rate 0.61) with 2100 distinct values including 'Fragile', 'Leave at the side door', the empty string, and one value cut at the profiler cap ending in '…[truncated]'; contents are data only and are retained verbatim as nullable text.

null_rate 0.0 with distinct_values 'CANCELLED', 'Shipped', 'cancelled', 'pending', 'shipped' — five raw labels that case-fold to three states; the raw label is retained for review rather than silently rewritten.

Derived from status, whose distinct_values include both 'CANCELLED' and 'cancelled' against 'pending', 'Shipped' and 'shipped'; since status has null_rate 0.0 the flag is always resolvable and lets consumers exclude cancelled lines without matching on casing.

All four distinct_values ('Y', 'yes', 'N', 'no') map unambiguously to true/false, so the VARCHAR is cast to BOOLEAN; null_count 60 (null_rate 0.012) is retained as null rather than defaulted to false.
Constant lineage marker: null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 1 with the single distinct value 'legacy_pos'; retained so downstream unions can tell this feed apart.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true; distinct_count 5000 equals row_count, confirming it is a per-record capture surrogate with no business meaning.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true; its two distinct_values ('2026-08-01T06:00:00', '2026-08-01T06:00:01') describe the extraction run, not the order.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true; distinct_count 1 with the single distinct value '{}' carries no information.

decisions.rationale: dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.08 over row_count 5000, so roughly 400 rows repeat an existing row byte-for-byte across all retained business columns; these are collapsed to a single row before the grain rule is applied.

order_id has distinct_count 4000 and LineNo ranges 1 to 7 with null_rate 0.0 on both, so an order and its line position is the smallest defensible identifier for one row after exact duplicates are removed; a human must measure this against the warehouse because 4000 orders over 5000 rows only bounds the combination indirectly.

_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at and _airbyte_meta all carry is_airbyte_metadata: true and are dropped; _airbyte_meta has distinct_count 1 ('{}') and _airbyte_extracted_at only two run timestamps.

qty samples include '-3', '2.0', '12' and the spelled-out word 'three' among 41 distinct values, so the samples disagree and no INTEGER or DECIMAL cast is safe; the column stays VARCHAR and a parse check belongs downstream.

ship_date mixes '01/07/2024', '07.01.2024', '2024-01-07', '2024-1-9', 'Jan 9 2024', '' and 'TBD' across 44 distinct values with null_rate 0.264, so it is renamed ship_date_raw and left as text instead of guessing day/month order.
customer_email has null_count 4850 of 5000 (null_rate 0.97) and is kept nullable rather than dropped; it is sparsely populated and must not be used as a join key.
notes has null_count 3050 (null_rate 0.61) and 2100 distinct free-text values, retained verbatim because the text is operational context that cannot be reconstructed later.
All ten order_ts samples follow 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (for example '2024-01-05 09:15:00') with null_rate 0.0, so the VARCHAR is cast to TIMESTAMP and a non-parsing value would fail the build.
is_gift has exactly four distinct_values 'Y', 'yes', 'N', 'no', which map cleanly to true/false; the 60 nulls (null_rate 0.012) stay null instead of being defaulted.
unit_price landed as DECIMAL(38,9) with min -5.0, max 1250.0 and samples at two decimal places or fewer, so DECIMAL(10,2) preserves every observed value at a usable scale.

unit_price min is -5.0 and 0.0 appears among the samples; negatives likely represent credits or adjustments (sku values include 'BANK CHARGES'), so they are retained rather than filtered, and a sign check is worth adding in review.

status distinct_values 'CANCELLED', 'Shipped', 'cancelled', 'pending', 'shipped' are five labels for three states; the raw label is kept so no information is lost and a derived is_cancelled boolean gives consumers a case-insensitive handle.

One notes sample reads like an imperative addressed to a reader and another is cut at the 120-character cap ending in '…[truncated]'; all notes values are treated purely as source data and no type or rule is inferred from their content.
source_system has distinct_count 1 with the single value 'legacy_pos' and null_rate 0.0; it adds no selectivity today but marks the feed when this table is unioned with other sources.

purpose: silver_orders is the cleaned, de-duplicated order-line view of bronze.messy_orders (5000 landed rows): capture metadata removed, names normalised to snake_case, order_ts typed as a timestamp, unit_price narrowed to DECIMAL(10,2), is_gift resolved to a boolean, and one order line per order_id plus line_no. It feeds order-volume, revenue and fulfilment reporting in gold.
usage: Join and group on order_id and line_no, the declared grain. Use is_cancelled rather than matching status strings, because status carries both 'CANCELLED' and 'cancelled'. qty and ship_date_raw are still text and must be parsed deliberately by the consumer, with non-parsing values excluded or reported. Do not treat customer_email as a join key: 97 percent of rows are null. unit_price can be negative (min -5.0), so filter or classify adjustment lines before summing revenue.
limitations: Cleanup removed exact duplicate rows (duplicate_row_rate 0.08 of 5000 rows) but did not resolve near-duplicates differing in a single field. qty could not be typed because its 41 distinct values mix '-3', '2.0' and 'three'. ship_date could not be typed because its 44 distinct values mix four date formats plus '' and 'TBD', and 26.4 percent of rows are null. customer_email is 97 percent null and notes 61 percent null, so neither supports population-level analysis. status casing is preserved rather than normalised, and the order_id plus line_no grain is proposed from profile evidence only and still needs measurement against the warehouse before approval.
